thirteen_lens_dispositions.bounded_assessment: StrategicIdentityComponent and manual CaseSite Serde use the same grammar; public fixture variants permit invalid place association even when checked factories and decoded string reject it. A feature-generated CaseSite native decoder is a separately attributed historical finding requiring current ingress and native mechanism qualification.

Fixture kind, exact place and chapter or outbreak identifiers must agree as an association, not just as independently valid fields. Item placement, protected parts and occupancy are related; the normal 95e view derives protected parts from a matched placement, while raw generated DTOs themselves do not enforce that relation.

Three P16 objects and the separate pr-working manifest match their respective pinned 95e file objects; old and current read scopes are independently recorded. Preserve coarse versus exact place, legal case-site and camp identities, intended checked rejections, distinct native wire shape, and source-version qualifications.

CaseSiteId manual Serde funnels into validation and the place/fixture parsers validate associations; deriving default serialization instead would not by itself preserve these invariants. Generated SATS rows are generated wire artifacts, not manually editable boilerplate.

StrategicPlaceId and StrategicFixtureId distinguish referents and fixture kinds, and the venue enum represents closed kinds. Public fixture payloads still allow inconsistent combinations; optional placement/appearance may legitimately denote an unworn or nonparametric item.

StrategicPlaceId and CaseSiteId own different referent constraints; generic world-event IDs and public generated DTO primitives remain boundary representations, not evidence for a new competing owner. Actual server-side authority and consumer admission govern how far the existing type can be preserved.

Hex encoding doubles each component; a checked 87-byte ASCII settlement ID yields a 194-byte canonical place string while generic event validation caps at 192. This independently continues the prior 774 and peer finding with actual producer/receiver conditions, not a new unique count.

256-byte component, 4096-byte place and 192-byte event ID limits are distinct owning policies. Their incompatible accepted domains are linked, but no global narrowing or downstream truncation is justified. SDK 2.6.1 is a declared/locked dependency identity, not inferred resolved runtime state.

Canonical prefix/version/kind/hex strings are a closed native encoding parsed by explicit patterns; names and error strings are not automatically duplicate semantic authorities. CaseSiteId::from uses expect and an already assessed unplanned approved-action boundary condition; actual malformed request remains hypothetical.

The current strategic view copies strategic character, item, condition and typed side data into generated ConnectedPlayer records; the tactical server takes a batch, prepares scene recipient/position and then projects it. Place becomes String before a separate event envelope check; producer/consumer admission must be traced independently.

A view derives protected parts from the selected authored placement while transport includes both placement and parts; this alone does not prove unsafe duplicate authority. Chapter fixture institutional identity can intentionally share an effective service venue, and is not the same as the venue itself.

Case-site, settlement shell, venue, chapter, residence, journey camp, component, fixture and event identifiers encode different scopes. Signed quantities and incidental DTO fields should not be wrapped indiscriminately without native and producer contract evidence.

Schema and view own generated field definitions; the authorized workflow regenerates bindings from schema when implementation is separately allowed. Tactical server owns transient hydration; strategic existence, visibility and authorization remain with reducers. No generated file edit or tactical tick persistence is proposed.
